summary: The candidate fixes the reviewed stale-probe ABA sequence by comparing both registration generation and failure count, and its focused regression passes. It does not fully close session-state races: registration publishes new decode arguments before advancing the generation and clearing state, allowing a concurrent failure against the newly published session to be erased by the later registration cleanup. The underlying cause of the reported recurring 5P3D GLM5.2 NVIDIA/XCCL RoCEv2 transfer failures was not identified or reproduced.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate regression against the recorded base: 4 failed, 10 passed, 3 subtests passed. Failures included default-disabled probing, both stale-probe races, and absent registration-generation bookkeeping.
Candidate's focused regression: 14 passed and 3 subtests passed, including the reviewed equal-count ABA sequence.
Independent ordering cases: the reviewed equal-count ABA case passed, but registration bookkeeping erased a failure occurring after new arguments were published (1 failed, 1 passed).
Changed Python source and regression compile successfully.
Candidate diff reports trailing whitespace in six lines of its committed raw evidence logs; no product-source whitespace error was reported.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) was detected, but the race tests are CPU synchronization tests. No GPU computation was used as proof.

remaining_counterexamples: Registration stores decode_kv_args_table[session_id] before _mark_session_registered(). A concurrent transfer can consume those newly published arguments, record a failure, and then have that new failure removed by _mark_session_registered().

The recurring failures in the reported 5P3D GLM5.2 NVIDIA/XCCL multi-node RoCEv2 deployment remain unexplained and may continue; the candidate adds recovery behavior but does not identify or correct their underlying cause.
remaining_limitations: The source deployment requires NVIDIA compute capability 8.6, XCCL, eight devices per node, multiple nodes, RoCEv2, and GLM5.2 weights; the prepared environment provides one AMD gfx950 GPU and no stated model weights or multi-node fabric.
No native source changed in the candidate, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The deterministic tiny-Llama serving fixture cannot qualify GLM5.2, XCCL, Mooncake RDMA, or a 5P3D distributed topology and was therefore not used as substitute proof.
